items.action: Move to a fix pack newer than the last affected pack for your release (R2023x FP.CFA.2613, R2024x FP.CFA.2632, R2025x FP.CFA.2637, R2026x FP.CFA.2635); restrict network access to the Station Launcher App in the meantime.
items.details: CVE-2026-93664 is deserialization of untrusted data (CWE-502) affecting 3DEXPERIENCE R2023x through R2026x. Two companion OS command injection flaws, CVE-2026-77033 and CVE-2026-19732, score 9.9 each but need a low-privileged account first. No exploitation or public proof-of-concept has been confirmed.
items.summary: Dassault Systèmes disclosed three critical flaws in the Station Launcher App of its 3DEXPERIENCE platform on November 16, the worst (CVE-2026-93664) an unauthenticated remote code execution bug scoring a maximum CVSS 10.0.
items.title: Dassault 3DEXPERIENCE flaw scores a perfect CVSS 10.0 — unauthenticated RCE

items.action: Watch for your distribution's kernel security update fixing CVE-2026-99288 and apply it as soon as it lands; monitor exposed Linux servers for unexpected crashes in the meantime.
items.details: Red Hat assigned the flaw a CVSS score of 7.5. The vulnerability is in the kernel's TCP handling; details were published via The Register on November 16.
items.summary: A critical Linux kernel vulnerability dubbed NoisyTCP (CVE-2026-99288), discovered by researcher Hyunwoo Kim, allows remote attackers to crash servers without authentication and affects nearly all Linux distributions.
items.title: NoisyTCP: critical Linux kernel flaw lets remote attackers crash servers unauthenticated

items.action: If you run Batflat, take it offline or migrate — there will be no fix. At minimum, block or restrict access to the /contact endpoint and audit the host for compromise.
items.details: Submitted data in the /contact endpoint is not sanitized, letting a remote attacker send a crafted POST request and run arbitrary PHP code with www-data privileges. CERT Polska published an advisory on November 16.
items.summary: Batflat CMS versions 1.2.0 through 1.3.6 have an unauthenticated remote code execution flaw (CVE-2026-111559, CVSS 9.3) in the public /contact form, with public exploit code already on GitHub — and the project is no longer maintained, so no patch is expected.
items.title: Batflat CMS remote code execution (CVE-2026-111559) — public exploit, no fix coming

items.action: Watch for targeted phishing and fraud using cardmember details; monitor for any official statement from Mastercard before treating the claim as confirmed.
items.details: The group marked the incident 'NOT PAID — EXPOSED', indicating the data has been leaked. The claim is unverified and Mastercard has not been reported confirming a breach; treat the exposure as alleged until independently confirmed.
items.summary: On November 16, the ransomware group N0n publicly claimed to have compromised Mastercard and leaked cardmember program records, including full names, emails and mobile numbers for individuals in Middle East and Africa programs, plus issuing-bank and BIN linkage.
items.title: Ransomware group N0n claims data exfiltration from Mastercard

items.action: MSU students and staff should watch for credential-reset guidance from the university and monitor for identity-theft alerts; treat the claim as unverified for now.
items.details: The group publicly named the university's incident response chair, accusing him of ignoring their outreach. The claim is unverified — the tracker indexes operator-posted claims and does not host or verify the stolen data.
items.summary: The ransomware group Byod claims to have exfiltrated full personal information for 1.03 million current and former Michigan State University students plus staff data, a claim indexed by the Ransomware.live tracker on November 16.
items.title: Byod ransomware group claims theft of 1.03 million records from Michigan State University

items.action: Debenhams customers should change their password, enable two-factor authentication where available, and treat any password-reset email with suspicion — attackers hold live recovery codes.
items.details: The group first listed the victim anonymously as 'Company #189' on November 9, with an estimated attack date of November 9; the data is marked 'NOT PAID — EXPOSED'. The leak also includes shopper search sessions with typed queries and session identifiers.
items.summary: On November 16, ransomware group N0n published data stolen from UK retailer Debenhams, including 15,708 customer email addresses and 8,530 password-recovery codes captured from password-reset confirmation links.
items.title: N0n leaks Debenhams customer data and password-recovery codes

items.action: NBFCs, especially smaller ones, should audit systems against the CERT-In and Delhi Police advisories, enforce per-transaction limits, and monitor for dummy reference identifiers and mule-account patterns.
items.details: Delhi Police have arrested 20 people linked to mule accounts and seized ₹18 crore of the ₹65 crore before it left mule accounts as cash or crypto. CERT-In warned that fraudulent transactions carried dummy reference identifiers, exceeded per-transaction limits, and credited attacker-controlled mule accounts; its advisory noted agentic AI frameworks enable the attacks 'at machine speed'. Over 150 complaints have been filed by NBFCs across India in the same period.
items.summary: NBFCs across India have lost more than ₹300 crore in a spate of cyberattacks, with 12 NBFCs in Delhi-NCR alone losing over ₹65 crore in the last three months; a government advisory rated the severity 'critical' and noted threat actors may have used AI to cover their tracks.
items.title: NBFCs lose over ₹300 crore to cyberattacks; AI used to cover tracks

items.action: Watch for the November 19 deadline and any confirmation from Connectwell; treat the claim as unverified until then.
items.details: The group set a publication deadline of November 19, 2026 at 20:15 UTC unless the organization engages in negotiations. The claim is unverified.
items.summary: On November 15, the ransomware group PixelLeaks publicly claimed a cyberattack against Connectwell Industries Pvt Ltd, an Indian electrical terminal-block manufacturer, threatening to release business records including intellectual property and operational material.
items.title: PixelLeaks claims breach of Connectwell Industries, threatens to leak business records

items.action: Traders should verify export buyers and certification providers through official channels before paying for certificates; report suspected call-centre fraud on the National Cyber Crime Reporting Portal (1930).
items.details: Police recovered 34 mobile phones, eight laptops, 14 CPUs, 23 diaries, two cheque books and fake certificates. The racket surfaced from analysis of complaints on the National Cyber Crime Reporting Portal, which showed cheated money routed through mule bank accounts; an IndusInd Bank account linked to the firm was tied to a fraud complaint from Maharashtra.
items.summary: Delhi Police on November 16 busted a fake call centre in Dwarka's Sector 7 operating as 'Web Solutions Export', arresting 20 people who allegedly duped manufacturers and traders across India with promises of international buyers and fake certifications.
items.title: Fake call centre busted in Dwarka for defrauding traders nationwide
